snippet.title: Episode 07: Intro to Behavioural Interviews
snippet.description: In this video, we break down the goals, components, and best practices of Behavioural Interviews. While they are, for the most part, non-technical, you might find yourself faced with questions you don't feel ready to answer in an interview like this. This episode will help you understand what it's all about and how you can be genuine without shooting yourself in the foot.

snippet.title: Episode 06: Intro to Architecture and Systems Design Interviews
snippet.description:
In this episode, I walk through the context and goals of a systems design and architecture interview. If you're considering working for a tech company, you'll almost certainly be asked to tackle a high-scale systems design problem. This video explains why companies ask this of you, how to prepare for this interview mentally and emotionally, and what success or failure might look like.

A full write-up of this video is available here: http://jg.gg/architecture-and-systems-design-interview/

snippet.title: Coding Interview Problem: Largest Rectangle in a Histogram
snippet.description:
Episode 05 comes hot with histograms, rectangles, stacks, JavaScript, and a sprinkling of adult themes and language. Brace yourselves!

Full text-form code is available here: http://jg.gg/largest-rectangle-in-a-histogram-coding-interview-problem/

snippet.title: Coding Interview Problem: Permutation Generator
snippet.description: Follow along as we dive into the problem of creating a permutation generator using C++. We'll walk through an efficient, in-place solution that leverages lexicographic ordering and incrementation. A full text version of the code is available here: http://jg.gg/permutation-generator-coding-interview-question/

snippet.title: Coding Interview Problem: Calendar Conflicts
snippet.description: Jackson walks through a linear (O(n)) complexity solution to the problem of finding conflicts in a calendar represented as a list of start and end times. The video features code written in PHP. It's written in the style of a Google coding interview (or Facebook, Amazon, etc. company).

snippet.title: Coding Interview Problem: Dinner Party
snippet.description: In this episode we look at a combinatorial complexity problem related to selecting subsets of our friends to join us for dinner. Coding in Python, we go through the premise of the problem, how to think about the a recursive structure to solve it, and a full implementation of a recursive solution.

snippet.title: Coding Interview Problem: Least Disruptive Subrange
snippet.description: In this episode, I'll guide you through an entry level coding problem that you might face in an interview at a tech company. This video discusses the problem, goes through a complete coding solution to the problem. We finish up with a walk through of the logic to confirm we've got the problem right. Full text-form code and discussion available here: http://jg.gg/the-unqualified-engineer-episode-01/
